**Finding submitted — ASSIGN: deviation (fallback cure).**

- **What exists:** Only § 10.3 (p0063), a binding-effect/successors-and-assigns recital. It says nothing about who may assign, on what notice, or with whose consent.
- **Direction check:** The silence cuts against us — HDI could transfer this hosting/development arrangement (including to a Wilson's/Excelled-type competitor) with no consent obligation. Confirmed by search that there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing trigger anywhere (termination sits only in the § 2 anniversary notice mechanic and the § 1 delivery-failure right), so this is a fallback failure, not walk-away.
- **Target chosen:** Fallback, since the bargain fails all four fallback elements and a mutual formulation is the shortest complete fix; no affiliate no-consent carve-out was added, which would conflict with "other assignments require consent."
- **Edit:** One inserted sentence pair after § 10.3 — mutual successor assignment on written notice; any other assignment requires prior written consent, not unreasonably withheld. Existing § 10.3 text left verbatim.
